use_cases.title: SAP S/4HANA data migration reconciliation
use_cases.description: A practical control pattern for proving that in-scope SAP migration data reached S/4HANA with expected identity, values and child-object coverage.
use_cases.problem: Migration teams need more than record counts: changed technical IDs, repeating child data and transformed business values must still reconcile back to the intended source objects.
controls: address and sales-area child collection reconciliation
outputs: offline evidence bundle with CSV/XLSX/HTML details
use_cases.limitations: The mappings and SAP fields are synthetic placeholders. Replace them with project-approved scope, identity and transformation rules; do not treat the example as SAP standard truth.

use_cases.title: SAP Customer to Business Partner reconciliation
use_cases.description: Reconcile legacy SAP Customer data to S/4HANA Business Partner when keys change and addresses or sales areas repeat.
use_cases.problem: A Customer-to-BP migration is not a flat row comparison: the BP can receive a new technical ID while addresses, sales areas and other child collections still need object-level assurance.
use_cases.limitations: The fixture proves the reconciliation pattern, not a universal SAP Customer/BP data model. Project scope and child identities must be defined explicitly.

use_cases.title: Source-to-target data reconciliation
use_cases.description: Version the source-to-target comparison logic instead of rebuilding one-off SQL or spreadsheets for each migration wave.
use_cases.problem: Teams need reproducible evidence that source records arrived at the target with the right business keys and values, including missing, unexpected and mismatched rows.
use_cases.limitations: This small CSV example is intentionally simple. Large flat datasets should use the DuckDB path; changed identities or hierarchy require the corresponding contracts.

use_cases.title: CSV file data reconciliation
use_cases.description: Compare two CSV extracts with deterministic keys, tolerances and evidence that can be rerun in CI or cutover rehearsal.
use_cases.problem: File-based reconciliation often becomes a manual Excel task with no stable definition of what counts as a match or acceptable difference.
use_cases.limitations: CSV is an input transport, not the business model. Keys, scopes, normalizations and acceptance rules still need project ownership.

use_cases.title: Data migration reconciliation checklist as executable evidence
use_cases.description: Turn a migration reconciliation checklist into executable controls: scope, keys, counts, values, tolerances, exceptions and retained evidence.
use_cases.problem: A checklist can say what should be checked, but a release decision needs repeatable execution and evidence tied to exact inputs and rules.
use_cases.command: rac run examples/materiality/reconciliation.yaml --evidence build/materiality-evidence.json --report build/materiality-evidence.md --bundle build/materiality-bundle --no-fail-on-diff
use_cases.limitations: Materiality is a business policy, not an algorithmic default. Thresholds and critical fields must be approved for the migration scope.

use_cases.title: Cutover reconciliation and sign-off evidence
use_cases.description: Use governed reconciliation evidence to support cutover readiness without hiding accepted differences or rebuilding sign-off spreadsheets.
use_cases.problem: Cutover teams need to distinguish true failures from explicitly accepted exceptions while preserving who accepted what and whether the exception is still valid.
controls: passed outcome only after valid exception policy
use_cases.limitations: An accepted exception is not proof that a discrepancy is harmless. Approval authority and expiry rules belong to the project governance model.

use_cases.title: SAP MDG replication reconciliation pattern
use_cases.description: Apply the same current-authority versus target-state controls to an MDG replication extract and its S/4HANA target evidence.
use_cases.problem: A technically successful replication message does not by itself prove that the current governed master-data state exists at the target with the correct business identity.
inputs: MDG-approved source export adapted to the starter schema
use_cases.limitations: The repository does not claim an embedded MDG connector here. The page shows how to adapt the runnable Customer/BP starter to MDG-approved and target exports; message causality/monitoring evidence should be handled by the integration/operations layer.

use_cases.title: Control totals by company code, country or business unit
use_cases.description: Reconcile financial or inventory totals by organizational dimensions instead of relying only on row-level equality.
use_cases.problem: A migration can have the expected total row count while still moving value between company codes, countries, plants or other business dimensions.
use_cases.limitations: The finance fixture is synthetic. Real reconciliation must define authoritative currencies, valuation dates, organizational scope and tolerances before totals can support sign-off.

faq: What is reconciliation in a data migration?
It is the controlled comparison of source intent and target business state: coverage, identity, fields, aggregates and accepted exceptions, with enough evidence to reproduce the decision.
Is row count enough for migration reconciliation?
No. Counts can match while keys, values, child collections or organizational totals are wrong. Counts are one control among several.
How should changed SAP technical IDs be reconciled?
Use an explicit identity crosswalk or governed identity relation. Do not assume legacy Customer and target Business Partner numbers are equal.
Can reconciliation evidence be used for cutover sign-off?
Yes, as one evidence input. The release policy still needs explicit ownership, accepted-exception governance and scope completeness.
Does Reconciliation as Code move data?
No. It evaluates and evidences source/target state. Extraction, transformation and loading stay in the systems and tools that own those operations.
Can it compare SQL sources instead of CSV files?
Yes. SQLite and PostgreSQL query inputs are supported through runtime connection references; credentials are not copied into the YAML or evidence.
How does it handle millions of records?
The DuckDB backend performs joins, filters and aggregates in-engine and returns bounded evidence; CI includes a generated one-million-row reconciliation benchmark.
Does a green result mean production data is correct?
Only within the declared scope and policy. A result cannot prove fields, records or business rules that the reconciliation contract did not include.
